steps.title: Order chrome glass photomasks
steps.instruction: Email the AutoCAD .dwg file to a mask‑making company (e.g., HTA Photomask) and order two 5 × 5 in quartz glass photomasks: one for cell traps with ±0.25 µm tolerance and one for media channels with ±0.5 µm tolerance; print closed objects as clear, right‑reading‑down, chrome side down.

steps.title: Optional wafer cleaning
steps.instruction: If desired, sonicate the 100 mm silicon wafer in acetone for 15 min, rinse with methanol, sonicate in methanol for 5 min, rinse with isopropanol, sonicate in isopropanol for 5 min, then rinse with deionized water.

steps.title: Dehydration bake wafer
steps.instruction: Bake the wafer at 150 °C for 15 min, then allow a 15 min cool‑down to room temperature (RT).

steps.title: Photolithography Layer 1 (cell traps)
steps.instruction: Create the first SU‑8 layer for cell traps using the following substeps.

substeps.instruction: Place wafer on spinner chuck with alignment tool.
Flood wafer with SU‑8 2005 to cover entire surface.
Spin coat: 40 s at 3000 rpm, acceleration ≈3000 rpm/s (reaches speed in ~1 s).
Soft bake at 65 °C for 9 min; cover with Pyrex dish lid during bake and cool on lid for 3 min to RT.
Expose on EVG620 mask aligner with Layer 1 chrome mask, vacuum contact, dose 75 mJ/cm², no filter.
Post‑exposure bake at 95 °C for 2 min, then cool 3 min to RT under Pyrex lid.
Develop in SU‑8 developer (large Pyrex dish) for 2 min with gentle shaking; rinse ~10 s with fresh developer then ~20 s with isopropanol.
Blow dry with nitrogen spray gun.
Hard bake at 95 °C for 5 min, then cool 3 min to RT.
Measure feature height with a profilometer and inspect under a microscope; dimensions should be within ±10 % of design.

steps.title: Prepare wafer for Layer 2
steps.instruction: Cover alignment markers with Kapton tape and adhesive label square, trim excess tape, and keep tape on until after spin coating.

steps.title: Photolithography Layer 2 (media channels)
steps.instruction: Create the second SU‑8 layer for media channels using the following substeps.

substeps.instruction: Pour ~4 mL SU‑8 2010 onto wafer (or use recommended SU‑8 2015 two‑step spin: 500 rpm, 136 rpm/s for 10 s then 3000 rpm, 272 rpm/s for 40 s).
Spin coat: 40 s at 1450 rpm, acceleration ≈1450 rpm/s (or the two‑step SU‑8 2015 protocol).
Remove Kapton tape covering alignment markers with tweezers.
Soft bake at 65 °C for 15 min, then cool 3 min to RT.
Align Layer 1 to Layer 2 mask on EVG620: adjust X, Y, Θ knobs, focus lenses, correct Y and Θ half‑steps, fine‑tune X as needed.
Expose with Layer 2 chrome mask, hard contact, dose 125 mJ/cm².
Post‑exposure bake at 95 °C for 5 min, then cool 3 min to RT.
Develop in fresh SU‑8 developer for ~5 min with gentle shaking; rinse with developer then isopropanol, blow dry with nitrogen.
Hard bake at 95 °C for 5 min, then cool 3 min to RT.
Measure media‑channel height with profilometer and inspect; aim for within ±20 % of design and confirm trap‑channel alignment.

steps.title: Wafer silanization
steps.instruction: In a chemical fume hood, place the wafer in a vacuum desiccator, add two microcentrifuge tubes each containing 20 µL trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H‑perfluorooctyl)silane, start vacuum and expose wafer for 7 min; wear appropriate PPE.

steps.title: Prepare PDMS mixture
steps.instruction: Weigh 30 g SYLGARD 184 base and 3 g curing agent into a plastic weighing dish, mix thoroughly with a glass stir rod.

steps.title: Degas PDMS and pour onto wafer
steps.instruction: Place PDMS mixture in a vacuum desiccator for ~30 min to remove bubbles; wrap wafer in aluminum foil forming a bowl, pour PDMS over wafer, return to vacuum for another ~30 min until bubbles disappear.

steps.title: Cure and release PDMS
steps.instruction: Bake the PDMS‑covered wafer at 80–90 °C for at least 1 h (overnight optional); remove aluminum foil with a razor blade, gently peel PDMS from wafer, cut individual devices with a razor blade, and punch inlet/outlet ports using a 0.5 mm biopsy puncher under a stereomicroscope.

steps.title: Clean PDMS devices
steps.instruction: Rinse PDMS devices with ethanol then deionized water, blow dry with nitrogen or air; apply Scotch tape to the feature side, rub back‑and‑forth with a blunt tweezer to lift dust (repeat ≥4 times on feature side, ≥1 time on non‑feature side).

steps.title: Clean glass coverslips
steps.instruction: Clean glass coverslips with heptane, rinse with methanol, rinse with deionized water, and blow dry with nitrogen or air.

steps.title: UVO‑clean surfaces
steps.instruction: Turn on the UVO‑Cleaner, run empty for 5 min; then place cleaned glass slides and PDMS devices (feature side up) in the chamber and run for 3 min.

steps.title: Bond PDMS to glass
steps.instruction: Flip PDMS devices, bring feature side into contact with the UVO‑treated glass slides, and place the assembled devices in an 80–90 °C oven overnight to bond; use devices within two weeks for experiments.
